resources.string: Your numbers, your strap, and how NOOP works. All on this phone.
Choose Light, Dark, or follow your system. Dark is the signature near-black; Light keeps the same clean look on a bright canvas.
Optional, on-device wellness signals. Each is off by default, computed only on this phone from data you already have, and never a medical diagnosis.
Reads a coarse menstrual-cycle phase from your nightly skin-temperature shift, on this device only. Awareness only: not contraception, not a fertility predictor, not a medical service.
Adds a simple fluid log with a daily goal that adjusts to your effort. Tap to add a sip, cup or bottle and watch a progress ring fill. On this phone only. Nothing is synced.

After a sync, NOOP looks over your recent heart rate for a sustained, raised stretch that looks like exercise and offers to save it. It only ever suggests. Nothing is saved until you tap Save, and you can dismiss any suggestion. Deliberately conservative, so the odd workout may be missed. On this phone only.
Keep screen on during a workout

Holds the screen awake while you\'re recording a workout, so your live heart rate stays visible without the phone dimming. Only applies during a recording. The screen sleeps normally the rest of the time. Leaving it on does use a bit more battery, and means your unlocked screen stays visible for the whole workout, so flip it off if that\'s a concern.

Lets NOOP notice a fresh HRV dip while you\'re still and offer a minute to breathe. \"Stress\" here is an autonomic proxy from your own baseline, never a diagnosis. The strap gives one light confirming buzz; no push notification.
When a dip is detected, surface the check-in card on its own (rate-limited, quiet-hours aware). Off keeps it manual.
Share on-device signals with the Coach

When the opt-in Coach is set up with your own key, also include a short summary of your strongest on-device patterns and Lab Book markers in its context. Summary only; no raw data leaves your phone. Requires the Coach\'s own data consent first.
Charge is NOOP\'s daily readiness score, learned from your own HRV, resting heart rate and more over time. Your history stays.
Restarts the roughly 4-night build-up for Charge and your HRV baseline from tonight. Use it if a bad first week set your baseline off. Your history stays.
Experimental 5/MG probes and the shareable Trends report. Tucked away to keep the everyday screen tidy.

Live heart rate already works on a WHOOP 5/MG strap. These probes go further and try to coax more out of it. They are guesses, off by default, and only ever touch a 5/MG strap. WHOOP 4.0 is never affected.

On a 5/MG connection NOOP will send a puffin realtime-stream request after the handshake, and log what comes back. If you have a 5/MG strap, turning this on and sharing your strap log helps map the protocol. No effect on WHOOP 4.0.

WHOOP 5/MG straps hand a fresh app only live heart rate. The official app switches on the deeper streams (high-rate HR + motion + history) by writing a set of feature flags, a sequence two independent projects have documented. With this on, the button below sends that exact sequence to your strap. Unlike everything else here it does write to the strap, but it\'s reversible (it only changes which data the strap emits) and is the same thing the official app does. Experimental: it may do nothing on your firmware.
Needs the full encrypted bond: close the official WHOOP app and pair the strap to NOOP first (a live-HR-only link can\'t carry the unlock).
Put the strap on first. The deep stream is on-wrist only.
Wear the strap, tap once, then let it sync and share your strap log.
%1$d type-0x2F historical-offload frame(s) seen outside our sync. These are history (e.g. another app pulling the strap\'s backlog), not a live R22 stream.
Flags accepted, but the enable sequence doesn\'t start a separate live stream. The deep records arrive as part of the normal history sync.
This restarts the roughly 4-night build-up for Charge and your HRV baseline. Your history stays. Use it if a bad first week, like wearing it while sick, set your baseline off.
Charge baseline reset. NOOP will re-learn it from tonight. Your history stays, and it takes a few nights to settle.
Buzz your strap when these apps notify you. Everything runs on this device.
When on, NOOP taps your wrist for the apps you pick below, so you can leave your phone and still feel what matters.
Tap your wrist for incoming phone calls and strict best-effort VoIP calls.
Uses the same quiet-hours and worn-only rules.
Needs Phone permission; NOOP never reads numbers or call logs.
Phone permission was denied, so phone-call buzzing is off.
Detects call-style notifications from known calling apps.
Wrist delivery needs Notification Access so NOOP can read which apps notify you. Nothing leaves this device. Your choices are saved now and apply automatically once access is granted.
Fine-tune when alerts reach your wrist.
Skip alerts when the strap is off your wrist.

Also buzz for apps that aren\'t in the lists above (e.g. BeReal). Android doesn\'t let NOOP see every installed app, so this is how you cover the rest. Can be chatty; quiet hours and \"only when worn\" still apply.

Optional phone notifications, off by default. These arrive after your strap syncs and NOOP scores the data, so they land soon after, not the exact second you wake or finish a workout. Everything is worked out on this phone.
After last night is processed, a notification with your Charge and Rest. Posts once a day, after your strap has synced the night.
When a new workout syncs in, a notification with its Effort, duration and average heart rate. Shows up after the session reaches NOOP on the next sync.
Everything stays on this phone. Bring your history in once, then it\'s yours.

Recovery, strain, sleep and workouts, stored locally. Import a full WHOOP data export (.zip) from app.whoop.com → Data Management and it backfills your whole history in about a minute. Working now on Android.
Import HR, HRV, sleep, SpO₂ and steps from an Apple Health export. On an iPhone: Health app → tap your photo → Export All Health Data, then import the .zip here. Working now on Android.

Pull steps, heart rate, HRV, sleep, SpO₂, weight and workouts straight from Android\'s Health Connect. No file needed. On-device; it never overwrites richer WHOOP data, and writes nothing unless you opt in to sharing back below.
Re-pull new Health Connect data (e.g. Samsung Health → Health Connect) each time you open NOOP, if it\'s been longer than the interval below. Read-only; never overwrites strap data.

Write the metrics NOOP computes from your strap (resting HR, HRV, SpO₂, respiratory rate, heart rate, steps, active energy and sleep) into Health Connect so other apps can use them. Only NOOP\'s own values are shared. Imported data is never echoed back.
Share computed metrics back to Health Connect
Health Connect isn\'t set up on this device. Install it from Google Play, then return here to import.
Health Connect write access not granted.
This permanently deletes everything imported from Apple Health: heart rate, HRV, sleep, steps, workouts and more. Your live strap data is untouched. This can\'t be undone.

This permanently deletes every day, workout and sample stored under WHOOP on this phone — imported history and anything synced from a strap. Apple Health and Health Connect are untouched. This can\'t be undone.
Save a full backup to a folder you choose - point it at Google Drive / Dropbox for off-device sync.
Point a sync app (FolderSync / Autosync) or a desktop Drive / Dropbox client at that folder for off-device backup — NOOP only writes the local file.
NOOP needs file access to write backups to that folder. Grant it once — it survives reinstalls (unlike the old folder-picker, whose access was lost on every update).
Writes a fresh dated backup to your folder once a day at the time below, keeping the latest %1$d. Off by default - flip it on if you want it.
Older backups beyond this many are pruned, oldest first (≈ that many days of daily backups). For recovery: if data ever corrupts, grab the newest snapshot.
Roughly when the daily backup runs (best-effort — the system may slide it a little).
Backup failed - grant file access and try again.
Replace this device\'s data with one of your backups. This overwrites current data, so back up first if unsure.
Save a one-off file to move your data to another phone or share it. The .noopbak is the lossless restore file; the CSV is a WHOOP-format zip that re-imports on Android or Mac.
Newest first. Restoring replaces this device\'s data.
Replace all current data with %1$s? This cannot be undone.
Merging your data and restarting. A large backup can take a moment.
Backup exported. Copy it to another phone and use Restore there.
%1$s Re-import it via Data sources -> WHOOP import, on Android or Mac.
Steps, heart, sleep, body composition and VO₂ max - synced from the desktop app.
Nothing imported yet. On an iPhone: Health app, tap your photo, Export All Health Data, then import the .zip here in Data Sources.
